newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Television agrees name change.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Television agrees name change.

text.p: Scottish Television Plc shareholders on Friday passed a special resolution to change the group's name to Scottish Media Group Plc.
The name change was required after STV, the ITV company for central Scotland, acquired Glasgow-based Caledonian Publishing, which publishes The Herald and The Evening Times, last October.
"We are now the largest multimedia group in Scotland, as the new corporate name is designed to reflect," chairman Gus MacDonald told the annual general meeting.
He said programme sales so far in 1997 for its production unit, Scottish Television enterprises, remain strong.
While audience share has been hit by increased competition from cable, satellite and most recently Channel 5, the regional service remains the most watched channel in central Scotland.
MacDonald said sales revenue has risen at above the average achieved by the whole ITV network in the first four months.
Last year STV launched satellite service Sky Scottish -- a joint venture with BSkyB.
